{{< include ../_experimental.qmd >}}

A small [inventory](../tutorial/inventory.qmd) for a bench test: an interrogator, a 20 m patch cord, and a 1 km spool of fiber on a table, recorded by one acquisition. The [tunnel recipe](tunnel_inventory.qmd) covers a full deployment. `python -m dascore inventory init <directory>` writes a placeholder directory to start from; here the files are written directly.

```{python}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from textwrap import dedent

import numpy as np

import dascore as dc

files = {
    # A local grid in meters, since a bench has no useful latitude.
    "inventory.yaml": """
        object_type: Inventory
        coordinate_reference_system:
          authority: local
          code: lab
          name: lab bench grid
          coordinate_labels: [x, y, z]
          units: [meter, meter, meter]
    """,
    "resources/bench-das.yaml": "object_type: Interrogator\nmodel: TODO\n",
    "resources/patch-cord.yaml": "object_type: Cable\nname: 20 m patch cord\n",
    # Network LB, fiber array SPOOL, blank location code, acquisition DAS.
    "acquisitions/LB.SPOOL..DAS.yaml": """
        object_type: Acquisition
        data_category: DAS
        interrogator: bench-das
        gauge_length: 2.0
        spatial_interval: 1.0
        distance_map:
          acquisition_distance: [0.0, 1020.0]
          optical_distance: [0.0, 1020.0]
    """,
    "fiber_arrays/LB.SPOOL/attrs.yaml": "object_type: FiberArray\n",
    "fiber_arrays/LB.SPOOL/path/attrs.yaml": "object_type: OpticalPath\n",
    "fiber_arrays/LB.SPOOL/path/optical_components.csv": """
        object_type,distance_min,distance_max,name,container
        FiberSegment,0,20,lead-in,patch-cord
        Connector,20,,spool connector,
        FiberSegment,20,1020,spool,
        Terminator,1020,,spool end,
    """,
    # The spool sits at one place: two rows with the same position.
    "fiber_arrays/LB.SPOOL/path/geometry.csv": """
        name,optical_distance,x,y,z
        lead-in,0,0.0,0.0,1.0
        lead-in,20,5.0,0.0,1.0
        spool,20,5.0,0.0,1.0
        spool,1020,5.0,0.0,1.0
    """,
    "fiber_arrays/LB.SPOOL/path/labels.csv": """
        distance_min,distance_max,group,value
        0,20,section,lead_in
        20,1020,section,spool
    """,
}

root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "lab_inventory"
for name, text in files.items():
    (root / name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / name).write_text(dedent(text).lstrip())

lab = dc.inventory(root)
lab
```

Each file's name states its identity, and `dc.inventory` (or `python -m dascore inventory check`) validates the directory. A patch joins by its `acquisition_key`:

```{python}
patch = dc.get_example_patch(
    "random_das", acquisition_key="LB.SPOOL..DAS", shape=(1021, 100)
)
spool = dc.spool(patch).attach_inventory(lab)

on_spool = spool.select(section="spool")[0]
enriched = spool.enrich().select(section="spool")[0]

assert on_spool.get_coord("distance").min() == 20
assert np.all(enriched.get_array("x") == 5.0)
```

Every channel on the spool gets the same position, since the fiber is wound in one place. The [inventory reference](../tutorial/inventory_reference.qmd) lists the other fields each file can hold.
